Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
847 PM EDT Tue Oct 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for City of Alexandria.
No other changes were made.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Near record warmth and mainly dry conditions continue
  through Wednesday. 

- 2) A strong cold front moves through on Friday, bringing 
strong winds, the potential for thunderstorms, and then cold 
conditions in its wake for this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Near record warmth and mainly dry conditions continue
through Wednesday.

Weak high pressure nearby and mid-level ridging will continue to 
dominate the forecast heading into Wednesday. The high itself will 
slide offshore later today allowing the mid-level ridge to buckle 
heading into Wednesday. Meanwhile, a series of shortwave 
disturbances will quickly slide from west to east across northern 
portions of the forecast region as a cold front drops south from the 
Great Lakes and Ohio River Valley. This front will touch off showers 
and a few thunderstorms late Wednesday afternoon and evening, mainly 
in areas along and north of I-66/US-50 and US-48. A Marginal Risk 
(Level 1 out of 5) for severe weather remains in place for portions 
of western MD, eastern WV, and the VA Highlands Wednesday afternoon 
where better instability/shear will reside. Thunderstorm coverage 
overall will be isolated to scattered with damaging winds as the 
primary concern (especially west of the Blue Ridge (between 3-8pm)). 
Most locations will remain dry through Wednesday afternoon given the 
timing of the front and residual dry air to punch through as the mid-
level ridge slowly buckles. 

Before the front arrives, expect near record warmth this afternoon 
and again Wednesday. Highs today will reach into the low to mid 80s 
(mid 70s mountains). Lows tonight will fall back into the upper 50s 
and mid 60s. Highs Wednesday will be much warmer in the mid to upper 
80s and potentially low 90s for areas south and east of DC (mid 70s 
mountains).

Cooler conditions return briefly Thursday as more of a wedge like 
pattern settles in. This is due to a large surface high pressure 
system anchored over southern Ontario wedging south along the 
eastern face of the Appalachians. Expect cloudy conditions to 
prevail along with passing showers, especially across the central 
and southern 2/3rds of the forecast region. Highs will return closer 
to normal with most locations in the mid to upper 60s. The CAD will 
quickly erode Thursday night into Friday as winds switch back 
to the south/southwest ahead of the next front heading into the 
weekend. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...A strong cold front moves through on Friday, bringing 
strong winds, the potential for thunderstorms, and then cold 
conditions in its wake for this weekend.

A potent shortwave trough will approach from the Great Lakes on 
Friday. A strong area of low pressure will form just downstream of 
this trough and track northeastward into the St. Lawrence Valley 
over the course of the day. Southerly flow ahead of the system will 
advect an unseasonably warm and humid airmass northward into the 
area, with temperatures forecast to climb into the 80s and dewpoints 
reaching into the 60s. The system's cold front will move through the 
area Friday afternoon into Friday evening. The front will move into 
an environment with around 500-1000 J/kg of instability, so a line 
of thunderstorms may ultimately form along the front. If 
thunderstorms were to form, they may be capable of producing 
damaging winds, given the strong winds that will be in place just 
above the surface (around 40-45 knots at 850 hPa). Regardless of 
whether storms form or not, strong northwesterly winds are expected 
behind the system's cold front late Friday through Friday night and 
into early Saturday morning. Frequent gusts of 30-40 knots appear 
likely across the area in northwesterly flow, and some locations may 
even see some gusts above 40 knots. The Alleghenies and Blue Ridge 
appear to be the most likely locations to reach Wind Advisory 
criteria of 40 knots.

Strong cold advection will also accompany the gusty winds, with 850 
hPa temperatures plunging from in excess of 15C Friday morning to 
below 0C by daybreak Saturday. Some upslope rain showers appear 
likely Friday night in the Alleghenies, and some snowflakes may even 
mix in by late Friday night. Air temperatures are forecast to dip 
into the 40s for most Friday night, with 30s in the mountains. By 
daybreak Saturday, wind chills will be in the 30s at lower 
elevations, and 20s in the mountains. Northwesterly winds will 
gradually decrease through the day Saturday, with temperatures 
forecast to climb into the 50s (40s mountains). High pressure will 
build overhead Saturday night, resulting in clear skies and calm 
winds within what will already be a cool background environment. 
This will be a near ideal situation for radiational cooling. With 
dewpoints forecast to be in the 20s and lower 30s, it appears as 
though a freeze may be possible for many locations, especially to 
the west of the Blue Ridge. At least frost appears likely just about 
everywhere, and freezing temperatures could encompass the entire 
area outside of the immediate downtown areas in DC/Baltimore if 
cooler solutions were to verify. Frost/Freeze headlines will likely 
eventually be needed for much of the forecast area. 

Quiet weather conditions and a gradual warming trend in temperatures 
are expected for Sunday and Monday as high pressure moves offshore. 
High on Sunday and Monday will generally be in the 60s (50s 
mountains), with overnight lows in the 30s and 40s.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions expected this afternoon through Wednesday afternoon 
as weak high pressure resides nearby. A front will drop into the 
area from the north late Wednesday afternoon and evening bringing 
with it scattered showers and thunderstorms. This will lead to brief 
sub-VFR reductions between 20-03z/4-11pm. Overall confidence for 
thunderstorm activity over the I-95 corridor terminals is less than 
25 percent with higher thunderstorm probabilities of 25 percent or 
greater mainly west of MRB. The front drops south of the region 
Thursday before stalling in the vicinity of southeast and southwest 
VA. This will put us in more of a wedge-like pattern with on and off 
showers and widespread sub-VFR (cigs) conditions at most of the 
terminals. Winds will remain out of the south today at 5 to 10 kts 
with occasional gusts up to 20 kts. South winds continue tonight 
into Wednesday at less than 10 kts. Did mention LLWS along and west 
of MRB and SHD tonight 2KFT AGL at 35 kts. Winds will switch to the 
north and northeast Thursday at less than 15 kts in the wake of the 
frontal boundary. 

VFR conditions and gusty south to southwesterly winds are expected 
Friday morning. A strong cold front will move through Friday 
afternoon. A line of thunderstorms could potentially accompany the 
front, leading to a brief period of sub-VFR conditions. Strong 
northwesterly winds are expected behind the front late Friday 
afternoon through Saturday morning, with gusts of 30-40 knots 
possible at times. Continued VFR conditions are expected on 
Saturday, with winds remaining out of the northwest, but gradually 
decreasing in magnitude throughout the day.

&&

.MARINE...
Southerly channeling effects could bring gusts close to SCA 
levels (around 20 knots), but this likely won't be for a long 
enough period to require a Small Craft Advisory. Instead, Marine
Weather Statements are more likely to be issued for small 
crafts to exercise caution. 

Winds diminish tonight into Wednesday, with generally sub-SCA 
conditions. A front moves south across the waters Thursday morning, 
and this is likely to bring SCA conditions with gusts around 20 
knots for several hours. Winds do quickly diminish Thursday 
afternoon.

SCA level winds appear likely in south to southwesterly flow Friday 
morning. A strong cold front will move through Friday afternoon into 
Friday evening. A brief line of thunderstorms may accompany the 
front. Winds shift to northwesterly behind the front, and Gale 
conditions appear likely along/behind the front Friday evening into 
early Saturday morning. Winds will remain northwesterly on Saturday, 
but gradually decrease in magnitude through the day.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
South winds on Wednesday could result in elevated water levels at 
sensitive locations along the Chesapeake Bay. This could result in 
several stations reaching Action Stage, with Annapolis and Havre
de Grace forecast to be closer to minor tidal flooding during 
the Wednesday morning high tide. A surge of offshore (north) 
winds Thursday morning will bring water levels back down.

&&

DC...None.
MD...Coastal Flood Advisory until 10 PM EDT this evening for MDZ014.
VA...Coastal Flood Advisory until 1 AM EDT Wednesday for VAZ054.

MARINE...None.
